This contract covers the Palace Electrostatic backend: Route A/B lowering,
handoff, Slurm execution, strict result resolution and report summaries, and
the mesh controls both Palace facades share.

## Public surface {#candidate-surface}

The public backend object is `scgsim.palace.ElectrostaticSim`. Staged calls
expose geometry, terminals, solver configuration, mesh, config, handoff, and
result processing instead of hiding the workflow in one orchestration cell.

The intended visible sequence is:

```text
prepare shared GeometryPlan snapshot
-> set_plan
-> add exact-net terminals and physical grounds
-> configure Electrostatic
-> mesh / config
-> common handoff
-> resolve / results / report
```

Handoff preparation does not submit Palace. Generated local or Slurm scripts
execute explicitly and write a receipt that the resolver verifies. Slurm
scripts bind `#SBATCH --output` and `--error` to `logs/palace-%j.log` so the
scheduler does not also write `slurm-%j.out`.

Before a generated script starts the solve, the exact copied `config.json` is
passed to the selected Palace executable with its native `--dry-run` option.
Only a successful dry-run of those exact bytes establishes config/runtime
compatibility. The compatibility artifact and returned receipt preserve the
config hash and observed native GitTag. When the configured executable is
directly and truthfully resolvable as the Palace binary, its basename and
SHA-256 are also retained. SCGSim does not inspect behind a wrapper to discover
its hidden binary. GitTag, commit, and any available binary hash are provenance
for reproducibility and diagnosis; their presence or value is not a
runtime-eligibility Gate.

If this preflight fails, the returned receipt records
`execution_stage="config_compatibility"`, `solver_invoked=false`, its separate
preflight and pipeline exit codes, and `solver_exit_code=null`. Receipts use
`execution_stage="solver"` only after the solver command was actually invoked.

| Stage | Public method | Intended responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Shared source | `set_plan` | Bind the immutable shared source snapshot. |
| Terminal binding | `add_terminal` | Select a terminal by exact SGB net identity. |
| Physical Ground binding | `add_ground` | Select conductor components for Palace Ground by exact SGB net identity. |
| Problem controls | `set_electrostatic` | Declare Electrostatic-specific config controls. |
| Output identity | `set_output_dir` | Bind the mesh/config/handoff output location. |
| Route | `set_route` | Route B when never called; `set_route("A")` uses the `thin_film` profile, or pass an `approximation_profile`. Run it before `mesh()`. |
| Surface films | `set_surface_epr` | Declare surface films and their inset margins; run it before `mesh()`. Without it, no Surface EPR is computed. |
| Mesh controls | `set_mesh(...)` | Select the sizing recipe, mesher options, repair budgets and quality threshold. |
| Source/settings view | `input_summary()` | Return the detached input `mesh()` builds from (the plan with the simulation's vacuum region and route applied) plus the settings, with no file or native I/O. |
| Mesh | `mesh` | Build the SGB geometry, check it for fine structure, mesh it with `scgsim.meshing` and lower its groups to Palace attributes. |
| Convergence | `set_convergence` | Declare the criteria that decide when adaptive refinement has converged; see [the convergence declaration](#convergence-declaration). |
| Config | `write_config` | Write the Palace Electrostatic configuration for the reviewed mesh identities. |

These methods are public APIs.

Configuration setters are atomic with respect to this staged state. Airbox,
Surface EPR, and Eigenmode controls validate every supplied value before
changing any field. A validation failure therefore preserves the prior
configuration together with cached mesh, resolved-port, config, and handoff
state. A successful change retains the existing mesh/config invalidation
boundary; this does not change operational failures inside `mesh()` or
`write_config()`.

## Palace mesh controls {#palace-mesh-controls}

A model needs a vacuum region: `mesh()` raises `ValueError` before writing any
file when the plan declares none and `set_vacuum_region` was not called on the
simulation (or `plan.set_vacuum_region(...)` before `prepare()`).

`mesh()` builds the geometry with SGB, meshes it with `scgsim.meshing` and
writes the Palace mesh, so the mesh controls are the controls of that module.
Both Palace facades accept them through `set_mesh(...)`, with the same defaults.
Omitted arguments retain their current settings. A change that alters a setting
invalidates the mesh, config and handoff; an invalid proposed value leaves the
prior state intact.

::: {.callout-note title="SCGSim's meshing is not required"}
The XAO that SGB writes (in `geometry/`) can be meshed with another tool, and
plain Gmsh has been tried on SCGSim's single-die and flip-chip test models and
meshes them. This is not an officially supported flow, and this page does not
describe how such a mesh connects to the rest of SCGSim.
:::

Before the mesher starts, `mesh()` runs the meshing stage of `simulation_drc` on
the geometry it built. A refusing finding raises `scgsim.palace.SimulationDrcError`,
carrying the report with each finding's location, owner and fix, and no mesh is
made; warnings do not stop `mesh()`. The classes and limits are in
[What the meshing stage reports](../layout-modeling-check.qmd#what-the-meshing-stage-reports).
The mesh controls below apply to a model that passed.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Control | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `recipe` | `FeatureRecipe()` | Chooses the initial element sizes: `FeatureRecipe`, `GlobalSizeRecipe`, `UniformBoundaryRecipe` or `GmshDefaultRecipe`. |
| `mesher` | `MesherOptions()` | Gmsh algorithms and the order of the delivered mesh: `algorithm_2d` (Gmsh's default when `None`), `algorithm_3d` (Delaunay), `geometry_order` (1) and `high_order_optimize` (`True`). |
| `budgets` | `Budgets()` | When the repair loop gives up: `max_rounds` (8 refinement rounds), `max_tetrahedra` (2,000,000) and a time limit of `time_limit_seconds` (180 s) for a model of at most `time_reference_area_mm2` (4 mm²) in x by y, growing in proportion above that area. The limit decides whether a round may start and how long its worker may run; writing the round's request and reading its result are not counted, so a result can arrive later than the limit by that much. `time_target_seconds` (60 s, scaled the same way) is reported, not enforced. |
| `quality_threshold` | `0.01` | The minimum signed inverse condition number (minSICN) every tetrahedron must reach. |
:::

Import `FeatureRecipe`, `GlobalSizeRecipe`, `UniformBoundaryRecipe`,
`GmshDefaultRecipe`, `MesherOptions`, `Budgets` and the `DELAUNAY` and `HXT`
algorithm constants from
`scgsim.meshing`. The repair policy is not a Palace control: Palace always uses
the module's default `RepairPolicy`.

::: {.callout-important title="A mesh below the quality threshold stops the run"}
`mesh()` raises `scgsim.meshing.MeshRepairError`, carrying the quality report,
when the repair loop cannot bring every tetrahedron to `quality_threshold`
within `budgets`; only `GmshDefaultRecipe` delivers such a mesh. It also raises when the mesh needs more than
`max_tetrahedra`, when the time limit is reached (a round still running is
stopped), when the count of bad elements has not fallen below its lowest for
two rounds in a row (`stalled`), when the accepted mesh cannot be raised to
`geometry_order`, or when Gmsh produces no mesh. No mesh path is returned, so
config and handoff preparation cannot continue. The report names the stop
reason, the time limit and the bad elements that remain; it is written to the
run's `mesh` folder, and the last mesh, if a round made one, stays there as a
`.rejected.msh` file.

When this happens, read where the remaining elements are. A stall usually
points at geometry the mesher cannot repair, such as an edge or a face one grid
step wide; fix it in the layout. Otherwise choose a recipe that sizes the
offending region finer, raise `Budgets.max_rounds` or the time limit, or lower
`quality_threshold` and record the lower value with the study.
`Budgets(max_rounds=0)` runs a recipe once without repair; it turns off repair
only, so a first mesh below the threshold is still rejected.
:::

### Sizing recipes {#palace-mesh-recipes}

A recipe decides only the initial element sizes. Repair, the threshold and the
report are the same for every recipe except `GmshDefaultRecipe`, which reports
the quality without enforcing it. Start with `FeatureRecipe`: it sizes the
curves the geometry itself calls for, and its defaults were measured to reach the
default threshold on 1 to 4 mm chips and, with Surface-EPR bands, on a flip-chip
qubit and on Route A sheets.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Recipe | Sizes | Parameters (defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| `FeatureRecipe` | A coarse maximum size, the bounding-box diagonal over `max_size_divisor`, with finer elements at thin film sidewalls (a multiple of the film thickness when that is finer than half the coarse size) and on every Surface-EPR band boundary curve (a multiple of the narrowest band width of its face; see [Band boundary curves](#palace-mesh-band-edges)). An optional rule sizes the outlines of the conductors. | `max_size_divisor=20`, `gradation=1`, `film_sidewall_thickness_multiple=25`, `film_sidewall_ceiling_fraction=0.5`, `conductor_outline=False`, `conductor_edge_size_um=5`, `conductor_edge_grow_um=300`, `band_mesh_size_multiple=4` |
| `GlobalSizeRecipe` | Only the coarse maximum size, the bounding-box diagonal over `max_size_divisor`. A cheap reference that leaves near-flat tetrahedra at thin metal sidewalls, so it relies on repair rounds. | `max_size_divisor=20`, `gradation=1` |
| `UniformBoundaryRecipe` | Every curve of the model at `near_um`, growing to `far_um` over `far_um` micrometres. It ignores what each curve is. | `near_um=5`, `far_um=300` |
| `GmshDefaultRecipe` | No size of its own: Gmsh meshes the model once with its own defaults, with no maximum element size and no repair. The mesh is delivered whatever its minSICN, which the report records, so it carries no quality guarantee; the tetrahedron and time budgets still apply. It is never the default: choose it with `set_mesh(recipe=GmshDefaultRecipe())`. | None |
:::

Each recipe has a name and a version, recorded with its parameters in the mesh
manifest, so a run states which sizing rules produced its mesh. A recipe's
version changes only when the sizes it asks for change; see
[Version identities of a mesh](../mesh-quality.qmd#version-identities).

#### Band boundary curves {#palace-mesh-band-edges}

With Surface-EPR margins, the largest mesh element on each Surface-EPR band
boundary curve is `band_mesh_size_multiple` times the narrowest band width of
its face. Like every size of `FeatureRecipe`, that size is rounded down to the
coarse size over a power of two, so with margins of 0.5 and 1 µm (bands 0.5 µm
wide) the default of 4 asks for 2 µm and gets 1.1 to 2.0 µm, depending on the
model's extent. A model without bands has no band boundary curves, and the
multiple changes nothing there.

Bands of 0.5 µm next to elements tens of micrometres long leave near-flat
tetrahedra that repair does not clear. On Route A no film wall is sized near a
sheet's edge, so without a size on the band boundary curves a single-die pad on
Route A stalls below the threshold. On Route B the film walls already set fine
sizes beside the bands; there the rule left no bad element in the first mesh of
the flip-chip qubit, which needed a repair round without it.

Keep the default of 4: of the measured multiples it is the only one that meets
the time target on the banded flip-chip qubit, and it meshes every measured case
clean. Set another multiple with
`set_mesh(recipe=FeatureRecipe(band_mesh_size_multiple=...))`:

- **A smaller multiple** (2) gives better-shaped elements at the bands, with a
  minSICN of 0.08 to 0.23 on the pad and the chips, but 1.8 to 2.4 times the
  tetrahedra of 4. The banded flip-chip qubit then does not mesh within the time
  limit.
- **A larger multiple** (8) saves elements only where band boundary curves set the size.
  On Route A it about halves them, but the minSICN of the pad falls to 0.014
  to 0.019, close to the default threshold. Next to Route B film walls it saves
  nothing:
  the flip-chip qubit gets the mesh it would have without the rule, needs a
  repair round and takes twice as long as with 4.

Measured with Gmsh 4.15.2, the default threshold and budgets, one model at a
time on an otherwise lightly loaded 64-core workstation (Gmsh uses one thread);
the rows of 2 were measured beside other work. On a busy machine the same runs
took up to half as long again:

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Multiple | Flip-chip qubit with bands | Single-die pad on Route A with bands | 1 to 4 mm chips with bands |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1.39 million tetrahedra; stopped at the time limit | clean; 216,000 to 235,000 tetrahedra; 14 s | clean; 23,000 to 37,000 tetrahedra; 1.6 to 2.0 s |
| 4 (default) | clean in the first mesh; 569,325 tetrahedra; 53 s | clean; 89,000 to 115,000 tetrahedra; 4.7 to 5.5 s | clean; 13,000 to 20,000 tetrahedra; 1.0 to 1.2 s |
| 8 | clean after one repair round; 407,093 tetrahedra; 105 s | clean; 49,000 to 52,000 tetrahedra; 2.6 to 2.7 s | clean; 9,000 to 14,000 tetrahedra; 0.7 to 0.8 s |
| No size on band boundary curves, for comparison | clean after one repair round; 407,093 tetrahedra; 83 s | stalls at minSICN 0.003 to 0.004 | clean; 9,600 to 13,500 tetrahedra; 0.7 to 0.8 s |
:::

The flip-chip qubit is the OrcaPen SC PDK `disk_flip_chip_qubit` under common
ground planes, Route B; the pad is `square_pad_capacitor` (200 µm pad, 1 mm
die). Bands are 0.5 and 1 µm on every metal-air, metal-substrate and
substrate-air face. The cases, every run and the machine load of each are in the
[band-edge measurement](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/blob/develop/experiments/meshing-benchmark/band_edge.md).

### Mesher options {#palace-mesh-mesher}

`MesherOptions` sets how Gmsh meshes whatever the sizes. Delaunay is the default
3D algorithm; `scgsim.meshing.HXT` is the alternative. Meshing runs on one
thread, and there are no thread controls.

`geometry_order` is the polynomial order of the delivered mesh, independent of
the finite-element order of `set_numerical(order=...)`. The audit, the threshold
and the repair loop always see the linear mesh. When `geometry_order` is above
1, the module raises the order of the mesh the loop accepted, optionally runs
Gmsh's `HighOrder` optimisation once (`high_order_optimize`), and writes that
mesh. A failure to fit curved elements raises an error; it is never replaced by
a straight or lower-order mesh.

## What `mesh()` writes {#palace-mesh-outputs}

The run folder holds the SGB model (`geometry/`, with the XAO and its sidecar),
the meshing report (`mesh/`, as JSON and text), `palace.msh` and the mesh
manifest (`metadata/`). `palace.msh` is a Gmsh MSH 2.2 ASCII file, the format
Palace reads. Palace lowers SGB's named groups to solver attributes from the
sidecar alone: it splits a surface group only where its faces are integrated by
different Surface-EPR rows or sides, so the attributes partition the faces and
nothing is counted twice. Electrical identity is the Net; the Terminal and
Ground bindings use the exact Net of the sidecar.

The meshing report states that minSICN and the count of tetrahedra below the
threshold were measured on the linear mesh before any elevation, and records
the order of the delivered mesh. Its fields are listed in
[The quality report](../mesh-quality.qmd#quality-report).

## Mesh manifest and detached summary {#mesh-manifest-and-detached-summary}

The mesh manifest (`schema_version` 2) records the route and its policy, the
sidecar schema and model identity digest, the Surface-EPR inset requests with
the band families they produced and the faces SGB skipped, the recipe (name,
version and parameters), repair policy, mesher options, budgets and threshold,
the path and SHA-256 of the quality report, and one entry per solver attribute
with the SGB group it came from. It also records the Gmsh version, node and
element types, physical-region element counts and edge-length statistics. Edge
lengths for high-order meshes are explicitly labeled as primary-corner chords
and reported in micrometres; they are not curved-edge arc lengths.

Both Palace facades and a resolved Palace run expose `mesh_summary()`. It returns
a detached value bound to the mesh and manifest identities. The Palace report
reads this same summary authority. Eigenmode includes an Nédélec topological
degree-of-freedom estimate based on primary-corner tetrahedron topology and the
configured FEM order. It is not an actual solver degree-of-freedom count;
changing FEM order updates the estimate without remeshing. Electrostatic's
H1 estimate is unavailable. No SCGSim record measures the quality of curved
high-order elements.

## Surface-EPR margins {#surface-epr-margins}

Surface-EPR inset margins are cut into the geometry as bands, so `set_surface_epr`
belongs before `mesh()`. The [Eigenmode contract](palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins)
owns the margin keys, the face kinds and the rows they produce, and Electrostatic
accepts the same specs. Surface EPR is optional here as in Eigenmode: without the
call, `mesh()` cuts no bands and the config has no Surface-EPR rows. Calling
`set_surface_epr` again, `None` included, invalidates the mesh, config and handoff.

## Source and geometry authority

Read the [SGB geometry concept](../concepts/geometry.qmd#source-stage) for the
source-to-construction explanation. The contracts below define the supported
preparation paths.

The simulation takes its source from `set_plan(snapshot)`, a prepared
`GeometryPlan`. The [GeometryPlan contract](../geometry-sgb.qmd) owns occurrence/Nets, generated
vacuum, contact and Route-A/B semantics. The current source-facing geometry
authority is `scgsim.geometry`. Palace builds its geometry with
`scgsim.geometry.sgb` (`build_sgb_geometry`) and meshes it with
`scgsim.meshing`. External SGB and gsim are derivation history only.

The [Electrostatic lesson](../course/palace-electrostatic.qmd) teaches exact Net
terminals/ground and the real mesh/config sequence. The separate
[Eigenmode contract](palace-eigenmode.qmd) defines mode and EPR output selection.
Neither preparation path starts Palace or submits a job. Shared private state
invalidation/persistence implementation lives in [architecture](../architecture.qmd#palace-preparation-lifecycle).

## Convergence declaration {#convergence-declaration}

`set_convergence(*criteria, minimum_converged_passes=1)` declares when an
adaptive run has converged. Both Palace facades take it. A criterion is a
quantity and a threshold; no threshold has a default:

```python
from scgsim.palace import Capacitance, ErrorIndicator, SurfaceEpr

sim.set_numerical(order=2, amr_max_passes=12)
sim.set_convergence(
    Capacitance.diagonal().within(relative=1e-3),
    Capacitance.element("island", "resonator").within(relative=1e-2),
    SurfaceEpr.each("MA", "MS", "SA", margin_um=1.0).within(relative=2e-2),
    ErrorIndicator().below(1e-2),
    minimum_converged_passes=2,
)
```

The numbers above only show the form; the thresholds are the user's.

| Quantity | On | Each pass reads |
|---|---|---|
| `Capacitance.element(a, b)`, `.diagonal()`, `.sub_diagonal(offset=1)`, `.off_diagonal()`, `.matrix()`, `.elements([(a, b), ...])` | `ElectrostaticSim` | Elements `C[a][b]` of the Maxwell matrix in `terminal-C.csv`, named by terminal. `sub_diagonal` pairs terminals `offset` apart in the order they were added; `off_diagonal` and `matrix` take each pair of different terminals once. |
| `ModeFrequency(modes=None)` | `EigenmodeSim` | `Re{f}` of each selected mode in `eig.csv`, in GHz; None selects every computed mode. |
| `SurfaceEpr(interface_kind, margin_um=None, modes=None, terminals=None)` | both | The participation of one interface kind: the sum over its whole-surface rows, or over its margin rows at `margin_um`. One number per mode (`modes=`, Eigenmode) or per excitation (`terminals=`, Electrostatic); None selects all. `SurfaceEpr.each("MA", "MS", "SA")` declares one criterion per kind with one threshold. |
| `ErrorIndicator()` | both | The `Norm` Palace writes to `error-indicators.csv`. |

`within(relative=...)` bounds the change from the previous pass,
$|q_k - q_{k-1}| / |q_k|$. When $q_k$ is zero the change is zero if $q_{k-1}$
is zero too, and otherwise undefined, so the criterion does not hold. The
absolute form names the unit the quantity is stored in: `absolute_f` for
capacitance (farads), `absolute_ghz` for frequency, `absolute` for a
participation, which has no unit. Give exactly one. `ErrorIndicator().below(value)`
bounds the value itself: the indicator is at most `value`.

A pass is one Palace solve: pass 1 solves the input mesh, and pass $k$ follows
$k-1$ refinements. A change criterion compares pass $k$ with pass $k-1$, so it
cannot hold at pass 1. A quantity with several numbers holds when each of them
does; the run has converged at pass $k$ when every criterion holds at each of
the `minimum_converged_passes` passes ending at $k$. The whole-surface rows and
the margin rows of a kind are never added together: a margin row is a part of
its whole-surface row.

::: {.callout-note title="What a change criterion says"}
A change criterion says that a quantity moved little between two passes, not
how far it is from its limit. On the layouts measured so far, whole-surface
participation grew at every pass, and no change criterion on it held, so such
a run goes to its pass limit. Participation beyond a margin (`margin_um=`)
did settle, though not steadily from pass to pass, which is what
`minimum_converged_passes` is for. The measurements are recorded on
[issue 248](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/248#issuecomment-6873586635).
:::

Another call replaces the whole declaration; `set_convergence(None)` removes it,
and `set_convergence()` with no criterion is refused. The call keeps the mesh
and discards the config and handoff, as `set_numerical` does.

### Checks

`set_convergence` refuses, naming the call to change:

- a quantity the simulation does not take (a `Capacitance` on `EigenmodeSim`,
  a `ModeFrequency` on `ElectrostaticSim`, `modes=` on Electrostatic or
  `terminals=` on Eigenmode), with the quantities the class takes;
- a threshold that is not positive and finite, or two thresholds, or none;
- `minimum_converged_passes` that is not an integer of at least 1.

`write_config()` refuses, before it writes anything:

- a terminal name the simulation does not have, or a selection with no element;
- a mode beyond `num_modes`;
- an interface kind with no Surface EPR requested (`set_surface_epr`), or one
  `set_epr_request(surface_interfaces=...)` leaves out;
- a `margin_um` its spec does not declare, naming the margins it does;
- an `amr_max_passes` too small for the declaration to hold at all: a run of
  `amr_max_passes` refinements solves `amr_max_passes + 1` times, and the
  declaration needs `minimum_converged_passes` solves, plus one when a criterion
  is on a change;
- a stated `amr_tolerance`, with the `ErrorIndicator().below(...)` criterion to
  declare instead;
- `save_adapt_iterations=False`, since every pass is read.

### What is written, and how it relates to the AMR controls

With a declaration, the declared criteria take the place of Palace's own
tolerance. `write_config()` writes `Model.Refinement.Tol` as the smallest normal
double, so that only `amr_max_passes` ends the run, and
`SaveAdaptIterations: true`, so that Palace keeps every pass in
`results/palace/iteration<k>`. It writes the plan of the check to
`metadata/palace_convergence_plan.json`: for each criterion its label as the
report shows it, and for each number the result table, the row, the columns and
how they combine (a participation sums the columns of its rows), the test, the
threshold, and `minimum_converged_passes`. Which columns make up a quantity is
decided there once, from the index map entries the same config writes.
`prepare_handoff()` seals the plan with the other inputs, so a returned run with
a changed plan is refused. Without a declaration nothing of this is written and
the config is what the AMR controls alone give.

### The stop at convergence {#convergence-stop}

With a declaration, no pass runs after the declared criteria have converged.
The run script starts Palace through the convergence runner that
`prepare_handoff()` copies into the run folder,
`metadata/run_palace_until_converged.py`, which needs only Python's standard
library ([execution profiles](../execution-profiles.qmd#convergence-runner)).
The runner:

1. starts the solver command the script would have run, in a session of its
   own; Palace's output reaches the log as before;
2. looks at `results/palace` every second. A pass counts once its
   `iteration<k>/` folder is unchanged between two looks, and after each new pass
   the runner runs the same check that result reading runs;
3. when the verdict is converged, writes
   `metadata/palace_convergence_decision.json` first, then sends SIGTERM to the
   solver's session. If the solver is still running 60 s later, it sends SIGKILL;
4. when the solver has ended, after the stop or by itself at `amr_max_passes`,
   writes the decision record again with the passes `results/palace` then holds
   and the solver's exit code.

The runner does not leave the solver running unwatched. Told to end (SIGTERM,
SIGINT or SIGHUP), it ends the solver first and records why. Ended without that
chance (SIGKILL, to the runner or to the script's whole process group), it
leaves the solver to its guard: a process the runner starts with the solver, in
a session of its own, which ends the solver's session in the same way once the
runner is gone.

Palace 0.18.1 completes pass $k$ in `iteration<k>/` before it refines the mesh
for pass $k+1$, so the stop comes during that refinement or at the start of the
next solve; no file of a completed pass changes. The cost is the time between
the folder and the look, one to two seconds, and none of the solves after it.

The receipt states how the solver ended (`ending`) and keeps the solver's own
exit code:

| `ending` | When | Receipt |
|---|---|---|
| `solver_ended` | Palace ended without a stop from SCGSim | `completed` when every exit code is 0, `failed` otherwise |
| `stopped_at_convergence` | the runner stopped it after a pass at which the verdict is converged, and it ended within the wait | `completed`, with the exit code the stop gave (Palace under `mpirun` exits 1) |
| `stop_escalated` | it did not end on SIGTERM and was killed | `failed` |
| `runner_terminated` | the runner itself was told to end, and ended Palace first | `failed` |
| `not_recorded` | the runner left no complete decision record | `failed` |

The result of a run stopped at convergence is its last pass: result reading
takes the tables and the cost from `iteration<k>/`, since the top level holds
links into it or a solve under way. Result reading computes the check again
from the returned files and refuses the run, naming what disagrees, when:

- the passes or the verdict differ from the decision record, or the record is
  not the one the receipt binds;
- the top level holds links or a solve under way, and the receipt says Palace
  ended by itself; or it holds a solve of its own, and the receipt says the
  runner stopped Palace;
- a decision record is present without a plan, or a plan has none.

`ResolvedPalaceResult.convergence` and the
[trust report](../report-model.qmd#declared-convergence) say at which pass the
run converged and where Palace stopped, or which criterion still fails at the
pass limit and by how much. `ResolvedPalaceResult.solver_end` (a `SolverEnd`)
holds the receipt's `ending`, the pass the runner stopped Palace after, and the
passes the limit allows (`amr_max_passes + 1`).

## Electrostatic defaults {#candidate-electrostatic-defaults}

These are implementation defaults, not universal scientific
recommendations or adequacy Gates:

| Control | Default value |
|---|---|
| `save_fields` | `0` |
| `unassigned_conductor_policy` | `"ground"` |
| `exterior_boundary_policy` | `"none"` |
| `Model.Refinement.Nonconformal` | `false` unless the notebook sets `amr_nonconformal=True` |
| `Model.Refinement.SaveAdaptMesh` | omitted unless the notebook sets `save_adapt_mesh=True` or `False` |

`sim.numerical` holds these controls as a `NumericalControls`: read a control
as a field (`sim.numerical.amr_nonconformal`) and the whole record with
`sim.numerical.to_payload()`, the dictionary
`metadata/palace_numerical_controls.json` holds. `sim.surface_epr_specs` is a
`SurfaceEprSpecs` (`sim.surface_epr_specs.by_type["MA"]`, or `to_payload()`
for the normalized mapping). A `NumericalControls` given to
`ElectrostaticSim(numerical=...)` gets the Electrostatic defaults above for the
AMR controls it does not set (0 passes, conformal, tolerance 0.01), as
`set_numerical(...)` does. With a [convergence declaration](#convergence-declaration)
the default tolerance is set aside and a stated one is refused.

Palace defaults `Nonconformal` to `true` when the key is omitted. SCGSim always
writes the key and defaults it to `false` (conformal tet AMR). Notebooks opt
into nonconformal AMR with `set_numerical(amr_nonconformal=True)`.

`set_numerical(save_adapt_mesh=...)` accepts only `True`, `False`, or `None`.
`None` (including omission) preserves the previous SCGSim numerical payload and
config bytes by omitting `SaveAdaptMesh`; a Boolean writes that exact Boolean to
`Model.Refinement.SaveAdaptMesh`. The control asks Palace whether to save its
final adapted mesh. It does not guarantee that a file is produced for every
solver run or private workflow.

`add_ground(net_id=...)` is the explicit physical-conductor path. It is
independent of `exterior_boundary_policy="ground"`, which adds the finite
solution-domain exterior faces. With `unassigned_conductor_policy="error"`,
every conductor component must be covered by exactly one Terminal or explicit
Ground binding. The index map records physical-Ground and exterior-Ground
attributes separately and their exact union must equal
`Boundaries.Ground.Attributes`. Existing
`exterior_boundary_policy="none"` plus
`unassigned_conductor_policy="ground"` remains the implicit-ground path.
Electrostatic authoring writes index-map schema v3, which carries the
physical-versus-exterior Ground split. The resolver reads only the current index
map and mesh manifest schemas; the
[report contract](../report-model.qmd#palace-run-schemas) states what happens to
a run folder of an older schema.

External gsim and historical SGB revisions are derivation evidence only. The
runtime geometry authority is the in-tree `scgsim.geometry.sgb` and the
current `scgsim.palace` implementation.

See [GeometryPlan and SGB](../geometry-sgb.qmd),
[Headless Geometry Preview](../geometry-preview.qmd),
[Execution Profiles and Local/Manual-HPC Handoff](../execution-profiles.qmd),
and [Provenance and Data Boundaries](../provenance.qmd) for the surrounding
contracts.
